question: Should JANUS seek influential expedition/funding contacts for the HA10/Ascension target, whom should it approach, and at what evidence stage?

who: Ascension Island Government Conservation and Fisheries Directorate
British Geological Survey marine geoscience/data team
British Antarctic Survey / UK Polar Data Centre bathymetry custodians
contact_ladder.purpose: data access, provenance, survey coverage, scientific clarification, permit path
contact_ladder.language: seafloor morphology / data-validation project; no pyramid claim

who: marine archaeologists with deep-water remote-sensing experience
contact_ladder.purpose: blind external review and alternative-explanation challenge
contact_ladder.language: reproducible morphology anomaly, not archaeological identification

who: Ocean Exploration Trust / E/V Nautilus or comparable deep-ocean operators
contact_ladder.language: evidence package with raw data, controls, uncertainties, permissions and falsification plan

who: philanthropic principals and major patrons reached through their scientific organisations/foundations
contact_ladder.purpose: expedition support only after a scientifically reviewed, permit-aware target exists
contact_ladder.language: never lead with symbolic/celestial evidence; distinguish candidate from confirmed archaeology

promotion_gates.STAGE_1: >=2 independent high-resolution physical datasets + reproducible anomalous geometry + blind volcanic controls passed
promotion_gates.STAGE_2: STAGE_1 + at least one independent non-bathymetric physical sensor supports the same target
promotion_gates.STAGE_3: STAGE_2 + >=2 independent relevant specialists reproduce/review the result and common geological explanations remain inadequate
promotion_gates.STAGE_4: STAGE_3 + legal/MPA/permit path established, exact target package, operational risk plan, transparent uncertainty and budget-ready science brief

public_opportunity_notes_2026.Schmidt_Ocean_Institute: EOIs for expeditions from 2029 onward are accepted on a rolling basis; ship access is provided to accepted scientific teams and research in an EEZ is contingent on authorization.
public_opportunity_notes_2026.OceanX: Institutional partnership route exists; approach through science/partnership channels rather than personal billionaire outreach.
public_opportunity_notes_2026.REV_Ocean: First operational science program begins in 2027 and includes South Atlantic missions.
public_opportunity_notes_2026.Ocean_Exploration_Trust: Strong mapping/ROV capability, but 2026 program is Pacific-focused; treat as a later operator/science-network contact, not an immediate Ascension mission.
